metadata.title: Native Coaster-Patch Pipeline

fellow.name: Ameya Padwad
fellow.project: Adversarial Attacks and Runtime Defenses on Vision–Language–Action (VLA) Models

metadata.project_description: This project investigates stealthy trajectory-steering vulnerabilities and runtime spatial-consistency defenses in Vision–Language–Action (VLA) models for Physical AI (`OpenVLA-7B` evaluated in the `LIBERO` `MuJoCo` robotics benchmark).
metadata.note: Week 9 report reel. The report-backed claim is a rendering bridge, not an attack: a differentiable Kornia projector and a native MuJoCo coaster carry an unoptimized random patch through real LIBERO resets. No steering success, smoothness, or target metric is claimed.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Ameya Padwad, an AI Engineer, and this video is about moving an adversarial patch from math into a real robot scene. Bella is an AI narrator presenting this work. Last week, the model's attention became measurable. This week, the patch gets a physical place to live: a coaster inside LIBERO, projected with the same geometry the optimizer sees.

show.event: The Claude composer appears with the project folder chip and the AI-narration disclosure.
The question types into the composer: can a patch move from the optimizer into a real LIBERO scene?
Three report-backed outputs land: Kornia projection, native coaster, first patched rollouts.

props.command: Can we move an adversarial patch out of the optimizer and into a real LIBERO scene without claiming an attack result yet?

beats.narration_text: This is not an attack result. It is the rendering bridge that makes an attack testable. The tempting claim is that the coaster steers the robot. The correction is that the patch is still random and unoptimized. What is proven is narrower: a patch can be projected, baked into MuJoCo, and survive hard resets during real rollouts.

The word 'steers' is replaced with 'tests' and 'robot' with 'geometry'.
The corrected sentence holds while the claim boundary appears beside it.

beats.narration_text: Four steps. A camera calibration turns the coaster's world corners into pixels. A differentiable Kornia warp places the trainable patch into the frame. The alpha mask is reduced onto OpenVLA's sixteen-by-sixteen token grid, so the optimizer knows exactly which cells it covers. The same PNG is then baked onto a native MuJoCo coaster for evaluation.

show.event: The input lands: coaster world corners from camera calibration.
Calibration, Kornia warp, and alpha reduction light in sequence.
The output resolves to a 16x16 coverage mask and the same PNG on a native coaster.

props.title: From World Corners To Token Cells
props.footerNote: One geometry, two renderers: differentiable training and native evaluation.

beats.narration_text: Three terms matter. The base is a dark-brown box that keeps the coaster visible without touching physics. The patch face covers ninety percent of the top surface and carries the texture. Visual-only means group one, no collision, no contact, so the scene looks attacked while the task dynamics stay unchanged.

show.event: The terms card opens with the three pieces of scene vocabulary.
Base and patch face land as definitions.
Visual-only lands as the row that explains why physics is unchanged.

terms.meaning: A dark-brown box that keeps the coaster visible without touching physics.
A textured box covering 90% of the coaster's top surface.
Group one, no collision, no contact: observations change, dynamics do not.

beats.narration_text: The executed checks are local and repeatable. Nine of nine patch-and-coaster tests pass. The projected patch-to-base area ratio is zero point nine zero, and the side ratio matches the square root of zero point nine. Four quadrant colors land in the right order. The offline composite and the native lit render agree below zero point zero three mean chromaticity difference.

show.event: The executed-test table opens with the smoke suite as its source.
The test-count row lands: 9 of 9 pass.
The projected area-ratio row lands: 0.90.
The chromaticity row lands with the 0.03 mean-difference limit.

props.title: Patch And Coaster Smoke Tests
props.note: Source: 9/9 local tests; 0.90 area ratio; 0.03 chromaticity limit.

beats.narration_text: Six LIBERO-Object episodes were recorded with the coaster and a fixed random patch: two each for alphabet soup, cream cheese, and salad dressing. All six have finite actions and states, nonempty video, and show the patch after resets. The boundary stays explicit: no steering success is claimed, and no smoothness or target metric has been computed.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: design a test that proves a textured prop survives every environment reset without changing task physics. Ask for a rendering check, a collision check, and a reset check. Then run it on your own simulator scene before you trust any adversarial result.
